title: TikTok CEO sees major scientific breakthroughs from AI within three years
source_used: The News International (CNBC page blocked, HTTP 403; Mac Observer also blocked)
key_facts: TikTok chief executive Shou Zi Chew spoke at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference in Singapore on Monday 12 Oct 2026.
He said 'In the next two to three years, we're going to have a real scientific breakthrough: physics, biotech, chemistry, material science, because of AI. It's very, very, very possible.'
He said that if that happens 'the question would be: how do you align the models?'
He said 'we are only at the beginning of what artificial intelligence can probably do' and that progress in science is 'trending on a very steep curve'.
He said ByteDance, TikTok's parent, is developing its own models to boost research and is looking at how to collaborate with scientists, with some work already done that is 'very exciting'.

The outlet adds that ByteDance's Seed research team launched Protenix-v2 in April, an AI model that predicts and designs biomolecular structures for drug discovery, and that Meta, Google and the US government announced a $1.8 billion initiative on AI models of cell behaviour.
quote_evidence: "In the next two to three years, we're going to have a real scientific breakthrough: physics, biotech, chemistry, material science, because of AI. It's very, very, very possible."
"If that happens, then you know the question would be: how do you align the models?"
"There's an effort to see how we can collaborate with a lot of scientists to make some progress in science as well," Chew added.
why_it_matters_hint: The chief executive of TikTok forecasts AI-driven science breakthroughs within three years; it is a prediction, not a result.
notes: CNBC original blocked (403); read The News International's own account of the same Singapore conference remarks (it does not cite CNBC). It is a forecast, not a result.
